items.quote: We currently support using personal access tokens and OAuth access tokens during the authentication process.
items.why: Names PAT and OAuth tokens; no Bearer detail, no legacy-key or breadth info.

items.quote: Any integrations that allow other users to grant access to Airtable should use OAuth.
items.why: Says OAuth for third-party access to other users; consistent, but not the full auth-method list.

items.quote: You can access the OAuth integrations panel at [/create/oauth](https://airtable.com/create/oauth).
items.why: Points to the OAuth panel URL; implies self-serve access but not free, no review, or the requirements.

items.quote: Most properties are optional, but note that the Privacy policy URL and Terms of service URL must be provided before sharing your
items.why: States privacy and ToS URLs are required before sharing; covers the key requirement, not 'only' or self-serve free.
Says the API follows REST; nothing on records, webhooks, admin endpoints or airtable.js.

items.quote: The API is limited to 5 requests per second per base.
items.why: States the 5 req/s per base limit, one part of the claim; rest of the API description unsupported.

items.quote: The server is available to all users on all plans.
items.why: Says the server is available to all users on all plans; no URL, existence, or vendor-official detail.
Gives the exact server URL, implying existence; vendor-official status not stated.

items.quote: The Airtable API can be used to integrate your data in Airtable with any external system.
items.why: Describes API integration with external systems; says nothing about what Airtable is as a platform.
